name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=cursor, descriptor=move_right). Accurately reflects behavior: right-arrow (scancode 0x4D) battle cursor handler that advances the cursor one tile to the right (or scrolls the viewport right). No Ghidra address residue; no domain ID to preserve. Matches its mirror siblings fd2_cursor_move_left/up/down.
purpose: Right-arrow (scancode 0x4D) battle cursor handler: advance the battle cursor one tile right, scrolling the viewport when the cursor is near the right viewport edge.
logic_summary: x_limit = map_width_tiles - 1. If cursor_world_x != x_limit (not at map right edge): if cursor_screen_x < 0xB (cursor in left 11 columns of the 13-tile-wide viewport) OR view_window_origin_x == map_width_tiles - 0xD (window already at max horizontal scroll) -> inner-step: cursor_world_x++ and cursor_screen_x++, and if anim_phase == 0 return early (main loop will redraw). Else -> scroll: cursor_world_x++ and view_window_origin_x++ (cursor stays put on screen, world+window advance right). All non-early-return paths (including the no-op right-edge case) fall through to fd2_composite_battle_frame(0) to redraw. Horizontal mirror of fd2_cursor_move_down.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects: mutates battle cursor/viewport globals and conditionally repaints the battle frame.

comment_original_issue: Header was a bare stub (just the @-address banner with no description), inconsistent with its mirror siblings fd2_cursor_move_up/down/left which each carry a full behavior description.
notes: Decompile was fully clear (cyclomatic 5, 23 insns); no disassembly needed. Plate comment already contains a detailed, correct body pseudo-code description consistent with the refined src prose, so plate left unchanged. Callers (fd2_game_main_loop, fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated, fd2_wait_for_action_target_input) confirm battle-input cursor-move context. __CHK(8) is the Watcom stack-probe/check prologue, not game logic. Viewport is 13 tiles wide (0xD); inner-step threshold screen_x < 0xB = left 11 columns. Signed-ness of cursor_screen_x is documented at its global definition in this same file; not relevant to this function's naming/comment.
